title: Identifying and Correcting Label Bias in Machine Learning
abstract: Datasets often contain biases which unfairly disadvantage certain groups, and classifiers trained on such datasets can inherit these biases. In this paper, we provide a mathematical formulation of how this bias can arise. We do so by assuming the existence of underlying, unknown, and unbiased labels which are overwritten by an agent who intends to provide accurate labels but may have biases against certain groups. Despite the fact that we only observe the biased labels, we are able to show that the bias may nevertheless be corrected by re-weighting the data points without changing the labels. We show, with theoretical guarantees, that training on the re-weighted dataset corresponds to training on the unobserved but unbiased labels, thus leading to an unbiased machine learning classifier. Our procedure is fast and robust and can be used with virtually any learning algorithm. We evaluate on a number of standard machine learning fairness datasets and a variety of fairness notions, finding that our method outperforms standard approaches in achieving fair classification.

claims.text: Training a classifier on examples with biased labels weighted by w(x,y) proportional to exp(sum_k lambda_k c_k(x,y)) is mathematically equivalent to training on unbiased labels under a modified feature distribution.
Under Lipschitz continuity and compact support assumptions, weighted loss estimation achieves a consistency rate of O(n^(-1/(4+2D))) relative to the true unbiased labels.
For data lying on a d-dimensional Riemannian submanifold in R^D, the weighted estimator achieves an intrinsic consistency rate of O(n^(-1/(4+2d))) independent of ambient dimension D.
On the MNIST dataset with 20% introduced label bias, the proposed sample re-weighting method achieves 96.16% test accuracy.
On the Adult dataset under demographic parity constraints, the re-weighting method achieves a test fairness violation of 0.0037 with 16.51% test error.

limitations.text: Re-weighting training examples trades off training on unbiased labels for training under a modified feature distribution P_tilde rather than the original data distribution P.
The finite-sample estimation rate bound degrades exponentially with high ambient feature dimension D unless the data lies on a lower-dimensional submanifold.
Prior data pre-processing approaches that alter observed features or labels may be legally prohibited as training on falsified data.
Lagrangian constrained optimization approaches require non-differentiable constraint relaxations and can suffer from non-convergence or unstable training.

methodologies.name: Iterative Sample Re-weighting for Label Bias Correction
methodologies.description: An iterative procedure that learns constraint multipliers lambda_k via gradient steps on constraint violations and retrains off-the-shelf classifiers using sample weights w_i proportional to exp(sum_k lambda_k c_k(x_i, y_i)) without modifying features or labels.
